summary: Kisari Mohan Ganguli (1848–1908) was an Indologist who studied at Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held a post at the University of Calcutta. He studied under traditional teachers including Madhusudana Nyayacarya, Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha, and Gopinath Bhattacharyya.

Kitaro Nishida (1870–1945) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1891–1894). He served as Professor of Philosophy at Kyoto University (1912–1927) and taught at Otani University (~1928–1935).

Kiyoaki Okuda (born 1938) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1968–1973). He served as a professor at Shitennoji University (~1976–2003) and directed the Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute (attested 2000).

Kiyoshi Kato (1907–1956) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his BA at Otani University under Enga Teramoto. He held posts at Higashi Honganji in 1935 and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School in 1938.

Kiyoshi Okano (born 1956) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University, including associate professor (attested 2002) and professor (attested 2013–2024).
Kiyoshi Shimokawabe (born 1944) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral course at Rissho University, where he later held posts attested in 1990 and 2001.

Kiyotaka Kimura (born 1940) studied Buddhist studies and Sinology at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, served as President of Tsurumi University (~2001–2011), and taught at ICPBS (~2011–2016).

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held academic posts at Toyo Bunko, Hokkaido University (~1996–2005), and Tohoku University (~2005–2018).

Kiyozo Kazama (born 1928), a linguist and Indologist, studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and attended the University of Vienna. He held posts at Hosei University (~1958–1962), Nagoya University (~1962–1970), and the University of Tokyo (~1970–1989).

Klaus Karttunen (born 1951), an Indologist and linguist, earned his degrees from the University of Helsinki studying under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola. He held various posts at Helsinki, including Acting Professor (1982), and conducted research with the Academy of Finland.
Klaus Mylius (1930–2025) was an Indologist who held posts at Leipzig University (~1964–1992), Goethe University Frankfurt (~1993), and the University of Bayreuth.
Klaus Pinte works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and served there as a teaching assistant in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn (born 1938) is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held professorial posts at the University of Giessen (~1978–2004) and the University of Göttingen (~2004).

Klaus Wille (born 1953) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at the University of Göttingen (1996), the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1997), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009, 2018–2020).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Marburg and habilitated at Hamburg. He directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1993) and served as Professor at the University of Vienna (attested 2012–2013).
Klemens Karlsson is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Uppsala University under Peter Schalk in 2000.

Knut A. Jacobsen (born 1956), a religious studies and Indology scholar, studied at UC Santa Barbara (~1989–1994). He served as a professor at the University of Oslo (~1996–1999) and the University of Bergen (~1999).
Kobun Chino Otogawa (1938–2002) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Kyoto University, and later taught Reginald A. Ray.
Kodo Akino (1858–1934) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and later served as its president (~1921–1924).
